title: Rosemary and Maple Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Maple syrup replaces the sugar and fresh rosemary is infused in place of vanilla.
summary: A take on our classic custard in which maple syrup does all the sweetening and fresh rosemary is infused into the dairy instead of vanilla. Woodsy, gently herbal and caramel-like.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Infuse
steps.text: Heat the cream and milk to a bare simmer, add the rosemary sprigs, cover and hold on the very lowest heat for 20 min, stirring the base occasionally so nothing catches. Remove the sprigs.

steps.title: Mix the yolks
steps.text: Whisk the yolks with the maple syrup in the heatproof bowl until thoroughly combined.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Slowly add about a third of the hot rosemary dairy, a ladle at a time, whisking constantly, then pour it all back into the pan.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Stir over medium-low heat until it coats the spatula and the probe shows 77-80 °C; it must not boil.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Season with the salt, strain and cool over the iced water. Chill for at least 4 h, or overnight for the best texture.

steps.title: Churn and freeze
steps.text: Churn until thick, then freeze for several hours until it holds a scoop.

tips: Use pure maple syrup; maple-flavoured syrups are mostly corn syrup and taste flat.
A common mistake is boiling the rosemary hard, which turns the flavour piney and harsh. Keep it at the barest simmer.
Serve with roasted pears or apples.
storage: Freeze, covered, for up to 2 weeks.
